title: Cache Lifecycle and Invalidation
readerIntent: Understand lookup, population, invalidation, import/export interaction, and recovery.
priorKnowledge: Know the logical cache channel and authoritative source.
owner: Owning capability, cache policy, and configured provider
summary: A read computes a tenant-safe key, checks eligibility, returns a valid hit or loads the authority, and invalidates or refreshes entries after owned state changes.

sections.heading: Read flow
items: Resolve tenant, principal, module, operation, and channel.
Build a bounded namespaced key without sensitive raw values.
Return a valid hit or load from the authoritative owner.
Store only eligible results with configured TTL and serialization.
Record safe hit, miss, bypass, provider, and latency signals.

sections.heading: Invalidation
items: The owning successful state transition emits or invokes its invalidation contract.
Single-process providers clear local entries; distributed providers propagate required invalidation.
If invalidation assurance is insufficient for a security-sensitive channel, fail closed or bypass cache.
Restart, reconnect, and topology changes must not make cached data authoritative.

sections.heading: Data exchange
paragraphs: A finalized import invalidates or refreshes affected cache entries through the same ownership contracts as ordinary saves. Export may read through authorized services, but correctness cannot depend on a stale cache and export must never dump cache storage as authoritative data.
